newsitem.title: CANADA: SNC-Lavalin order backlog at C$2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: SNC-Lavalin order backlog at C$2.1 bln.

text.p: SNC-Lavalin Group Inc said on Friday that its order backlog rose to C$2.1 billion at December 31 from C$1.86 billion a year earlier.
The engineering firm said its order backlog in Canada was C$643.6 million at the end of the fourth quarter, compared with C$723.4 million a year earlier.
Its order backlog outside Canada rose to C$1.44 billion from C$1.14 billion a year earlier.
SNC-Lavalin said almost 57 percent of its 1996 revenues came from outside Canada, due mainly to the sluggish Canadian economy.

"The growth of our earnings was mainly attributable to an increase in revenues and gross margins on major international contracts, a positive contribution from Kilborn and containment of administrative expenses in a context of rapid growth," the company said.
Kilborn is a Canadian engineering firm specializing in mining and metallurgy, which SNC-Lavalin acquired in 1996.

"The significant contribution of Kilborn to our results and new contract awards, mainly in mining and metallurgy, reflects the soundness of our decision to acquire the company. We expect the same kind of results from Pingat, also acquired in 1996, and Pellemon, currently being acquired," SNC-Lavalin said.
Pingat Ingenierie is a French engineering firm specializing in the agrifood business, which SNC-Lavalin acquired in 1996.
